title: How to squat without shoulder pain
summary: NH explains why the high-bar squat position causes shoulder pain for many lifters and gives strategies beyond mobility work: don't squat after shoulder-heavy days, warm into the narrow grip gradually, warm up the shoulders, look for other root causes, and replace part of squat volume with shoulder-friendly variations like the safety bar squat.

claims.claim: Many lifters get shoulder pain getting into squat position, mostly due to poor mobility but also due to individual anatomy.
A narrow grip on the squat makes it easier to pack the upper back, tuck the elbows and get tight; the wider the grip, the harder that is.
He high-bar squats with elbows at his sides; when grinding out of the hole he drives the bar down into his back as if bending it over his traps, which creates upper-back tension and core rigidity.
Without a narrow grip you lose rigidity and thoracic extension, and the upper back can round, turning the squat into a good morning.
Don't schedule squats the day after heavy bench, trap or upper-back work: the shoulder girdle will be pre-fatigued and possibly inflamed, making it hard to get and hold position.
In his experience the low-bar squat taxes the elbows and wrists more than the shoulders; his advice targets the high-bar squat.
Squat after a rest day or after a day of accessories/arms; even heavy lower back work the day before can hurt the squat.
You can deadlift after almost any type of day except squats or deadlifts, but the squat needs more scheduling priority than the deadlift because the back-squat position is demanding on the shoulders.
Don't start warm-ups with your working grip: begin as wide as possible and narrow the grip set by set until you reach your working grip (pinkies on the rings for him).
You can also start warm-ups with a false (thumbless) grip, narrow it, then switch to a full grip once you reach the narrow position.
If you start a session with shoulder pain it tends to stay for the whole workout, so warming the shoulder up first matters.
Pain is partly mental: after serious injuries his doctor said were fully healed, he still felt pain because of his relationship with it.
Before touching the bar, do dynamic stretches, shoulder rotations or side raises to warm up the shoulders; but in some people pumping blood into the shoulder makes it more rigid and reduces mobility.
Don't fall for the mobility meme: squat-position shoulder pain may come from another exercise, like horizontal presses, felt only when the shoulder is cold in the squat setup.
Grip width on the squat depends on your proportions and preference; if you can go wide and stay tight, do it. Not everyone needs a narrow grip.
If you need a narrow grip but it hurts, replace about 50% of your squat work with belt squats, hack squats or, best of all, safety bar squats to let the shoulders recover.
Replacements need not be permanent: while the shoulders recover and you work on mobility and strength, you can return to high-frequency high-bar squatting pain-free.
